From 05e815539f3f161585c13a9ab023341bade2c52f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wan Jiabing <wanjiabing@vivo.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2022 17:41:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] cxl/core/port: Fix NULL but dereferenced coccicheck error

Fix the following coccicheck warning:
./drivers/cxl/core/port.c:913:21-24: ERROR: port is NULL but dereferenced.

The put_device() is only relevent in the is_cxl_root() case.

Fixes: 2703c16c75ae ("cxl/core/port: Add switch port enumeration")
Signed-off-by: Wan Jiabing <wanjiabing@vivo.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220307094158.404882-1-wanjiabing@vivo.com
Signed-off-by: Dan Williams <dan.j.williams@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/cxl/core/port.c b/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
index c1681248f322..2ab1ba4499b3 100644
--- a/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
+++ b/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
@@ -911,7 +911,10 @@ static void cxl_detach_ep(void *data)
 			break;
 
 		port = find_cxl_port(dport_dev);
-		if (!port || is_cxl_root(port)) {
+		if (!port)
+			continue;
+
+		if (is_cxl_root(port)) {
 			put_device(&port->dev);
 			continue;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

**Modifications in Each File:**

1. **File: `drivers/cxl/core/port.c`**
   - A condition was added to check if `port` is NULL before the existing check for `is_cxl_root(port)`. The line `if (!port || is_cxl_root(port))` was split into two separate checks:
     - First, if `port` is NULL, the loop continues with `continue;`.
     - The check for `is_cxl_root(port)` was retained but moved to a separate block, ensuring that `put_device(&port->dev);` is only called when `port` is not NULL and is a root.

**Relationships between Modifications:**

- The changes made in `drivers/cxl/core/port.c` address a specific issue detected by coccicheck that warned of potential dereferencing a NULL pointer. By first ensuring that `port` is not NULL before proceeding with further logic, the risk of dereferencing a NULL pointer is mitigated. This fix is particularly relevant when isolating `put_device()` calls to only apply in scenarios where `port` is valid (not NULL) and is a CXL root, aligning with best practices in memory safety and error handling in code.
